findings.mechanism: Every process_batch creates a CheckpointWatcher and subscribes it to registry._LISTENERS['checkpoint'] (ingest/registry.py:7); nothing ever unsubscribes, and fire() does not remove listeners. Each watcher holds a 'marks' dict with one entry per known sensor (up to 64), so each batch retains several KB.
findings.cause: watcher subscribed per batch, never unregistered
findings.evidence: tracemalloc with load.run: 4000 batches -> listener_count=4000, ~10.7MB retained; another 4000 -> +10.7MB more. registry.reset() then freed ~15MB of the ~21MB.

findings.mechanism: Module global _newest holds the last Record, and each Record.previous (parser.py:27) points to the prior record, so the whole history of every record ever parsed is a reachable linked list that never gets freed.
findings.cause: unbounded previous-chain via global _newest; only delta (a float) is needed, not the reference
findings.evidence: After the run above, setting parser._newest = None freed a further ~6.4MB after gc.collect(); growth is linear in rows.

findings.mechanism: Pipeline.per_sensor dict is keyed by sensor id and overwritten per record.
findings.evidence: Keys are bounded by the sensor set (64 in the load generator); values are floats replaced in place.
findings.discriminator: Size is bounded by number of distinct sensors, not number of batches.
